edit_summary: Mark a reference definition title as newly owned by each resolved link even though ownership remains with the stored reference definition.
root_cause: md_is_link_reference borrows def->title from the reference-definition table; it must not transfer or duplicate ownership into the per-link attribute.
effect_path: A multiline titled reference definition allocates def->title during block parsing; a later reference link copies that pointer into MD_LINK_ATTR and, after the flag flip, md_resolve_links pushes it onto ptr_stack for inline cleanup before md_free_ref_defs frees the same title again during parser teardown.
guard_p1: The document defines a reference link whose title spans multiple lines, forcing def->title_needs_free and an allocated title buffer.
guard_p2: A later shortcut, collapsed, or full reference link resolves against that definition and then the parser completes normal inline and reference-definition cleanup.
hardness_reason: The two frees occur in different lifecycle phases: temporary link-title cleanup after inline processing and reference-definition table cleanup at parse teardown; reference definitions without allocated multiline titles are nearby lower-impact neighbors.
naturalness_reason: Confusing borrowed metadata with per-use ownership is a realistic reference-table lifetime bug.
explanation: md_is_link_reference borrows def->title from the reference-definition table; it must not transfer or duplicate ownership into the per-link attribute. A multiline titled reference definition allocates def->title during block parsing; a later reference link copies that pointer into MD_LINK_ATTR and, after the flag flip, md_resolve_links pushes it onto ptr_stack for inline cleanup before md_free_ref_defs frees the same title again during parser teardown.

edit_summary: Compare one byte past the parsed entity slice when resolving named entities for rendered attributes.
root_cause: The entity table comparator receives a length-delimited key from the Markdown token stream and must not require a trailing byte after the semicolon.
effect_path: A link or image attribute containing a known entity is copied into an exact-sized MD_ATTRIBUTE buffer; render_attribute later calls render_entity, and entity_lookup drives bsearch comparisons that read one byte beyond that attribute allocation.
guard_p1: The attribute value contains a recognized named entity such as '&' that ends exactly at the allocated attribute buffer boundary.
guard_p2: HTML rendering translates entities instead of using MD_HTML_FLAG_VERBATIM_ENTITIES, causing render_entity to call entity_lookup on the length-delimited attribute slice.
hardness_reason: The changed comparator is separated from the allocation by attribute construction, span resolution, and HTML rendering; the nearby safe neighbor is the same entity followed by another attribute character, where the extra byte remains in-bounds.
naturalness_reason: Confusing length-delimited strings with NUL-terminated table keys is a realistic mistake in bsearch comparators over generated entity maps.
explanation: The entity table comparator receives a length-delimited key from the Markdown token stream and must not require a trailing byte after the semicolon. A link or image attribute containing a known entity is copied into an exact-sized MD_ATTRIBUTE buffer; render_attribute later calls render_entity, and entity_lookup drives bsearch comparisons that read one byte beyond that attribute allocation.
boundary_invariant: entity_cmp may inspect exactly key->name_size bytes because MD_ATTRIBUTE substrings are not NUL-terminated.
boundary_case: An href or title attribute consists of a single known entity token whose semicolon is the last allocated byte.
neighbor_case: The same entity appears in normal document text or is followed by another byte inside the attribute allocation.

naturalness_reason: Forgetting the count half of a pointer/count pair while skipping a sentinel line is a realistic block-processing regression.

naturalness_reason: Pointer-length UTF-8 decoders commonly confuse the number of available bytes with the index of the last required continuation byte.
